hard_constraints: Ben must NOT know Aevyn's name or identity in this scene.
Talon Veyr's name surfaces only via Dorrin's records check near the end of the scene; Ben must not anticipate it before the search returns it.
The fragment shows a duplicated shipment identity, a quarantine/survey disguise, Jacen's personal encryption marker, and a partial GAG logistics/audit trace. It is NOT enough to solve the case.
Ben learns the Iresh destination and Jacen's encryption marker only when he and Dorrin read the recovered fragment within this scene; he does not arrive already knowing them.
The vacated Coruscant Jedi Temple is visible on the skyline through corridor windows; Ben registers it but does NOT look at it twice.

Dorrin controls the scene and lets Ben in under limits because Elya's message makes him relevant and Luke has quietly vouched for the urgency. Dorrin is NOT a third lead, secret mentor, corrupt reveal, or doomed ally.

Ben senses Force-trauma in the office: precise, intimate, controlled. He recognizes the shape of it without being able to name it yet. This is NOT a fight or desperation; something systematic was done to a person who could not defend against it.

The fragment is hidden by Elya's records instincts in the gap behind a dark, decommissioned workstation's power-coupling housing (heat-degraded, exactly where she wedged it in Chapter 1, not an obvious safe). The killer searched but never found it.
Ben's old GAG service marker is the channel Elya used; Ben knew this marker still worked but told himself he would never have to use it.
No ABY/BBY dating in narration or dialogue. Characters reference events directly.
No 'Legends' or 'Canon' as in-universe concepts.
Star Wars vocabulary discipline: datapads not tablets, transparisteel not glass, durasteel not steel, turbolifts not elevators, comlinks not radios, blasters not guns.
'Jedi' is both singular and plural; never 'Jedis'.
Capitalize 'Human'; lowercase 'galaxy'.
Force prose is experiential and mystical, never clinical. Avoid 'energy field' framing.
Ben's Jacen-derived crisis logic surfaces as body-sensations first, named only after the body has felt them.
The fragment is not enough to solve the case. Dorrin can validate the official case context and preserve access, but he cannot interpret what the fragment means.
Dorrin's first records check points toward an old GAG personnel/prosecution trail Ben cannot interpret alone.
The GA Senate vote expelling the Order is context for why GA Justice controls a crime that touches a Jedi.
Ben's decision not to look at the vacated Jedi Temple tells the drafter and reader everything about his relationship to what Coruscant voted for.
canon_risks: Risk: Ben's Force-sense of the trauma might be described too clinically. Must be experiential: body-sensation, dread, recognition without naming.

Risk: The fragment's Jacen encryption marker might be described as 'Jacen's personal encryption' in narration before Ben and Dorrin read it. The marker is revealed through reading the fragment within the scene, not before.

Risk: Dorrin might be given too much GAG or Force knowledge. He is a GA Justice investigator assigned to sensitive old-GAG and political-crime cases, but he is NOT a GAG veteran or Force-sensitive. He cannot decode the fragment or interpret the Force-trauma.
Risk: The vacated Jedi Temple might be described with too much exposition. One beat, no dwelling; Ben's decision not to look at it is the entire treatment.

Risk: Ben's old GAG service marker might be described as 'obsolete GAG identity-address protocol' in narration. Use simpler reader-facing language: 'old GAG service marker' or 'deprecated routing code'.

Risk: The Force-trauma signature might be described as 'weaponized Recognition' or 'Jacen-derived method' in narration. Ben does NOT know these terms yet. Describe the sensation: precise, intimate, controlled, systematic, wrong in a way he knows without wanting to.
Risk: The fragment's Iresh destination might be revealed too early. Ben learns it only when he and Dorrin read the recovered fragment within this scene.

Risk: Dorrin's records check might surface Talon Veyr's name with too much detail about his GAG history or conviction. The check should surface the name, location (Tarn Velos), and a connection to manifest-authorization patterns close to the fragment, but NOT the full Glasshook backstory or Tess connection.

Risk: Ben's reaction to the Force-trauma might be described as 'recognition of Aevyn's method.' He recognizes the shape of it without being able to name it yet. The shape is familiar enough to disturb him because he knows it from the inside (Jacen's training), not because he knows who did it.
legends_continuity_notes: The GA Senate vote expelling the Jedi Order from Coruscant occurred at the end of Fate of the Jedi (44 ABY), after the Lost Tribe crisis. The Order relocated permanently to Shedu Maad in the Hapes Cluster. This is why GA Justice controls a crime that touches a Jedi.
The Coruscant Jedi Temple was vacated in 44 ABY. It is no longer Order property. Ben's decision not to look at it on the skyline is a wound specific to this post-exile era.
GAG was dissolved in disgrace after the Battle of Shedu Maad (41 ABY). Its records, personnel, and infrastructure were decommissioned, but some old channels and markers may still function.
Jacen Solo's personal encryption marker is a detail consistent with his GAG-era operational security. He personally encrypted sensitive orders and shipments.

Cale Dorrin is a GA Justice / Coruscant Security investigator assigned to sensitive old-GAG and political-crime cases. This is a plausible role in the post-war, post-exile Coruscant legal environment.
The fragment's quarantine/survey disguise is consistent with GAG-era methods of moving sensitive material under official cover.

Ben's old GAG service marker is a deprecated routing code from the wartime period. It rides standard HoloNet infrastructure but bypasses Jedi institutional comms. This is consistent with GAG's parallel communications network.
The Force-trauma signature Ben senses is precise and controlled, not savage. This is consistent with Jacen-derived methods (Recognition turned coercive) but Ben does not know the term yet.
Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works is a storm-lashed industrial coastal prison world. Talon Veyr is held there at story start.
The vacated Jedi Temple on the skyline is a specific post-FOTJ texture: the Order was pushed off Coruscant, and Ben is operating on a planet where the Jedi have no institutional foothold.
possible_disney_bleed: Avoid 'Inquisitorius' as a formal post-Imperial organization (Disney Canon structure). Legends Inquisitorius is Empire-era only and not relevant here.
Avoid 'World Between Worlds' (Disney Canon Force concept from Rebels).
Avoid 'kyber crystal bleeding' mechanic (Disney Canon lore). Legends Sith use synthetic crystals.
Avoid 'Ben Solo' naming. 'Ben' in this novel is unambiguously Ben Skywalker.
Avoid 'High Republic' references (Disney Canon publishing initiative).
Avoid 'sequel trilogy' entities (First Order, Resistance, Starkiller Base).
Avoid 'The Way' as Mandalorian creed (Disney Canon convention). Legends Mandalorians follow Resol'nare.
Avoid 'Ahsoka Tano' post-Rebels characterization (mostly Disney Canon).
Avoid 'Mortis' naming on-page. The Crucible aftermath is implication only.
Avoid 'energy field' as a description of the Force. Use experiential, mystical language.

Elya's body has been removed but the chair, terminal, and blood smear on the terminal edge remain. Daytime overhead lighting now, harsh and fluorescent. Other Bureau offices on the floor have been cleared for the investigation.

allowed_au_divergences: Aevyn Soris is a NEW character: marginal Force-sensitive, Jedi-rejected at fourteen, joined GAG as a young adult, became Jacen Solo's side-project Force student during the Caedus period while Ben remained the primary fourteen-year-old apprentice.
Jacen's unfinished holocron is a NEW artifact: a working device assembled during the LotF period, systematizing Recognition and Holding.
The duplicated wartime quarantine/survey shipment manifest personally encrypted by Jacen Solo shortly before the Battle of Shedu Maad is a NEW canonical artifact specific to this novel.

Iresh and the Glasswell are NEW locations: Iresh preserves charged impressions of memory, identity, and decision under pressure. The Glasswell is a natural sinkhole/cavern beneath a mirror-lake lined with pale translucent mineral. NOT a Sith temple or Jedi ruin.
The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation (public charity), the Vigil (hidden inner ring), and Greyline Strategic Services (Tess's firm) are NEW post-war Coruscant-political institutions.
Cale Dorrin is a NEW character: GA Justice / Coruscant Security investigator assigned to sensitive old-GAG and political-crime cases. Grounded official contact only.
Tarn Velos Coastal Detention Works and Civitas Archive Systems are NEW Book 1 settings.
Legacy comics future (Darth Krayt galactic war, Cade Skywalker, fall of GA) is EXCISED. The One Sith remain in pre-emergence on Korriban.
Allana Solo / Amelia is treated as a dangerous gray zone in adversary awareness only, referenced obliquely in Ch 37. Never named on-page in Book 1.
open_questions: Is the exact layout of the third-floor records office at the Coruscant Bureau of Post-Conflict Logistics specified in any Legends source? If not, the drafter may invent it as needed.

Is the exact nature of the 'blood smear on the terminal edge' consistent with Elya's death method (weaponized Recognition)? The method kills by pushing mind and body past survivable limits; physical trauma may be minimal. The smear should be consistent with a precise, controlled death, not a violent struggle.

Should the fragment's hiding place (behind a decommissioned workstation's power-coupling housing) be described with any specific technical detail about GAG-era equipment? The drafter may keep it simple: 'heat-degraded gap behind a dark, decommissioned workstation's power-coupling housing.'

Is there any Legends-era precedent for GA Justice / Coruscant Security investigators handling sensitive old-GAG cases? If not, the drafter may treat it as a plausible post-war institutional development.

Should Ben's recognition of the Force-trauma shape be explicitly linked to Jacen's training in this scene, or left as a vague dread? The scene card says 'he knows the shape of it without being able to name it yet.' The drafter should keep it as body-sensation and dread, not explicit naming.

Is the exact timing of Ben's arrival (half a day after Elya sent the message) consistent with travel time from Shedu Maad to Coruscant? Shedu Maad is in the Hapes Cluster, multiple hyperspace jumps from Coruscant. Half a day is plausible for a fast ship with a good hyperdrive.

Should Dorrin's records check surface any other names or details beyond Talon Veyr? The scene card specifies only Talon Veyr's name, location, and connection to manifest-authorization patterns. The drafter should keep it focused on Talon.
